## About

This course teaches graduate students how to move from biological sequence data to defensible environmental bioinformatics interpretation. Each student develops and completes a research project targeting a reproducible final compendium by the end of the quarter. The weekly topics emphasize bioinformatics data types and analyses; computing tools such as RStudio, Quarto, GitHub, Raven, and Hyak are learned in stages and used throughout the quarter.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: callout-important
## Do this before Week 1

1. Complete **Tutorial 1** on the [Setup](setup.qmd) page (your computer: shell, Git, GitHub). About one hour.
2. Create your course repository from the [project template](https://github.com/course-fish546-2026/project-template) in the course organization.
3. Open a **Project Proposal** issue on the [course repository](https://github.com/sr320/course-fish546-2026/issues/new/choose). A rough draft is fine; you will refine it all quarter.

Raven comes online in Week 1 and Hyak in Week 3. You do not need them yet.
:::

Bioinformatics is not only running tools. It is the practice of keeping data provenance clear, choosing appropriate analyses, checking intermediate products, and making biological claims that the evidence can support.

## Format

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tuesdays** | 3:00–4:20 PM, FSH 203. Topic session: the week's bioinformatics concept and data type. Oct 6 – Dec 8. |
| **Thursdays** | 9:30–11:20 AM, FSH 203. Working session: apply the concept to your project. Oct 1 – Dec 10, no class Nov 26. |
| **Fridays** | 5:00 PM. Weekly notebook entry due (Mon Nov 30 for Thanksgiving week). |

This class is driven in part by student needs and is flexible in content. It is practical and problem-driven. The first meeting, Thursday Oct 1, is a setup working session.

::: {.callout-important style="color: orange"}
**Your repository is how we work.** Every week you do one analysis, write one notebook entry in your repository, push it, and post the commit link on your Project Proposal issue. The instructor replies there. That single loop is the whole course workflow; it is spelled out on the [How We Work](how-we-work.qmd) page. Be sure you have a GitHub account, are part of the course organization, and have notifications turned on. Day-to-day chat is on [Slack](https://genefish.slack.com).
:::

## Platforms

You will work across three computing tiers. They come online in stages; each has a [setup tutorial](setup.qmd).

| Tier | Platform | Role | When |
|---------------|--------------------------|--------------------------|------------|
| Your computer | Local shell + Git/GitHub | Editing, version control | Before Week 1 |
| Raven | RStudio Server at <http://raven.fish.washington.edu:8787> | **Home** for most weekly work | Week 1 |
| Hyak / Klone | HPC (SLURM + containers): `ssh <UWNetID>@klone.hyak.uw.edu` · [On-Demand](https://ondemand.hyak.uw.edu) | When Raven is not enough | Week 3 |

Course GitHub Organization: <https://github.com/course-fish546-2026>

## Textbook

[Bioinformatics Data Skills](https://www.amazon.com/Bioinformatics-Data-Skills-Reproducible-Research/dp/1449367372/) — Reproducible and Robust Research with Open Source Tools, by Vince Buffalo (O'Reilly, 2015). [Supplementary repo](https://github.com/vsbuffalo/bds-files).

## Grading

There is one deliverable each week: a **notebook entry** in your repository containing the week's analysis, answers to two or three reflection questions from the lecture, your project progress, blockers, and next week's goals. You will also give a mid-quarter project update and a final compendium presentation.

| Component | Grade % | Notes |
|--------------------------------|---------|--------------------------------|
| Weekly notebook entries (Weeks 1–9) | 60% | due Friday 5:00 PM; best 8 of 9 count |
| Presentations | 15% | mid-quarter update (Week 5) + final presentation (Week 10) |
| Final compendium | 25% | your repository at the Week 10 release |

**Weeks 1–4** use shared exercises so everyone practices the same core data types. **Weeks 5–8** apply each week's method to your own project data; a canned fallback exercise is provided when the method does not fit your project.

Rubrics for all three components are on the [How We Work](how-we-work.qmd) page.

**Late policy:** 40% deduction; not accepted more than 5 days past due.

## Core competencies

Skills in this course are anchored to the [**Roberts Lab Handbook**](https://robertslab.github.io/resources/) — its computing best practices, data management, and platform guides (Raven, Klone) are the reference standard for how you are expected to work.

## Weekly arc

The course moves from sequence identification and raw sequencing data toward multi-assay environmental interpretation. See the [Schedule](schedule.qmd) for each week's topic and analysis.

1.  Sequence databases and BLAST.
2.  Raw reads, FASTQ, quality control, and trimming.
3.  Mapping, alignment, assembly, and quantification.
4.  RNA-seq and differential expression.
5.  Genome annotation and genomic ranges. Mid-quarter update.
6.  Variants and population signals.
7.  DNA methylation and regulatory genomics.
8.  eDNA and metabarcoding.
9.  Project synthesis and biological interpretation.
10. Final compendium and presentations.
